bio|10-22|1990|Λουί Αλτουσέρ|Louis Althusser|Louis Althusser was a French Marxist philosopher. In his works "For Marx" and "Reading Capital" he proposed a structural reading of Marx. He died in 1990.

bio|10-23|1491|Ιγνάτιος Λογιόλα|Ignatius of Loyola|Ignatius of Loyola was a Spanish priest and theologian. He founded the Society of Jesus, the Jesuits, in 1540 and wrote the "Spiritual Exercises". The Catholic Church honours him as a saint. The exact year of his birth is uncertain. He died in 1556.

bio|10-23|1688|Δουκάγγιος|Du Cange|Charles du Fresne du Cange, known as Du Cange, was a French philologist and historian. He compiled dictionaries of medieval Latin and medieval Greek and studied Byzantium. He died in 1688.

bio|10-23|1872|Θεόφιλος Γκωτιέ|Théophile Gautier|Théophile Gautier was a French poet, critic and writer of Romanticism. He wrote "Mademoiselle de Maupin" and supported "art for art's sake". He died in 1872.

bio|10-23|1940|Πελέ|Pelé|Pelé, whose real name is Edson Arantes do Nascimento, was a Brazilian footballer. He won three World Cups, in 1958, 1962 and 1970, and played for Santos. He is regarded as one of the greatest of all time. He died in 2022.
bio|10-23|1944|Τσαρλς Γκλόβερ Μπάρκλα|Charles Glover Barkla|Charles Glover Barkla was an English physicist. He studied X-rays and in 1917 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics. He died in 1944.

bio|10-23|1946|Έρνεστ Τόμπσον Σέτον|Ernest Thompson Seton|Ernest Thompson Seton was a British-Canadian writer and naturalist. He wrote stories about animals and was one of the founders of the Scouting movement in the United States. He died in 1946.

bio|10-23|1957|Πολ Καγκάμε|Paul Kagame|Paul Kagame is a Rwandan politician. He was the leader of the rebels who put an end to the genocide of 1994, and he has been president of the country since 2000.
bio|10-23|1976|Ράιαν Ρέινολντς|Ryan Reynolds|Ryan Reynolds is a Canadian actor. He became known as "Deadpool" and appeared in the comedies "The Proposal" and "Free Guy".
bio|10-23|1986|Εμίλια Κλαρκ|Emilia Clarke|Emilia Clarke is an English actress. She became known as Daenerys Targaryen in the series "Game of Thrones" and also appeared in "Me Before You".
bio|10-24|51|Δομιτιανός|Domitian|Domitian was a Roman emperor from 81 to 96, of the Flavian dynasty. He was the son of Vespasian and the brother of Titus. He was assassinated in 96.
bio|10-24|996|Ούγος Καπέτος|Hugh Capet|Hugh Capet was king of France from 987 to 996. He was the founder of the Capetian dynasty, which ruled France for centuries. He died in 996.

bio|10-24|1601|Τύχο Μπράχε|Tycho Brahe|Tycho Brahe was a Danish astronomer. He made extremely accurate observations of the planets, which were used by the assistant of Johannes Kepler. He died in 1601 in Prague.

bio|10-24|1632|Αντονί βαν Λέβενχουκ|Antonie van Leeuwenhoek|Antonie van Leeuwenhoek was a Dutch scientist. He built microscopes and was among the first to observe bacteria and microorganisms. He died in 1723.

bio|10-24|1633|Ιάκωβος Β΄|James II|James II was king of England and Scotland from 1685. He was a Catholic and his policies provoked the Glorious Revolution of 1688, when he was deposed. He died in 1701 in France.

bio|10-24|1957|Κριστιάν Ντιόρ|Christian Dior|Christian Dior was a French fashion designer. He founded the house of Dior in 1946 and in 1947 presented the "New Look", which changed women's fashion after the war. He died in 1957.

bio|10-24|1985|Γουέιν Ρούνεϊ|Wayne Rooney|Wayne Rooney is a former English footballer. He played as a striker for Manchester United and the England national team and is the all-time top scorer in the history of Manchester United. He has also become a coach.
bio|10-24|1986|Drake|Drake|Drake, whose real name is Aubrey Graham, is a Canadian rapper and actor. He became known as an actor in the series "Degrassi" and then as a rapper, with major hits.

bio|10-24|2005|Ρόζα Παρκς|Rosa Parks|Rosa Parks was an American civil rights activist. In 1955 she refused to give up her seat to a white passenger on a bus in Montgomery, and this started the bus boycott. She died in 2005.
bio|10-25|1154|Στέφανος|King Stephen|Stephen was king of England from 1135 to 1154. His reign was marked by a civil war with Matilda, known as "The Anarchy". He died in 1154.

bio|10-25|1400|Τζόφρι Σώσερ|Geoffrey Chaucer|Geoffrey Chaucer was an English poet. He wrote "The Canterbury Tales" in Middle English and is regarded as the father of English literature. He died in 1400, according to tradition on 25 October.

bio|10-25|1647|Ευαντζελίστα Τοριτσέλι|Evangelista Torricelli|Evangelista Torricelli was an Italian physicist and mathematician. He invented the mercury barometer and demonstrated the existence of atmospheric pressure. He was a pupil of Galileo. He died in 1647.
bio|10-25|1806|Μαξ Στίρνερ|Max Stirner|Max Stirner was a German philosopher. His work "The Ego and Its Own" supports individualism and is regarded as a forerunner of anarchism. He died in 1856.

bio|10-25|1811|Εβαρίστ Γκαλουά|Évariste Galois|Évariste Galois was a French mathematician. He contributed to group theory and the theory of equations, known as Galois theory. He was killed in a duel in 1832, at the age of 20.
bio|10-25|1838|Ζωρζ Μπιζέ|Georges Bizet|Georges Bizet was a French composer. He wrote the opera "Carmen" and "The Pearl Fishers". He died in 1875, at the age of 36.

bio|10-25|1881|Πάμπλο Πικάσο|Pablo Picasso|Pablo Picasso was born in Málaga, Spain, and lived in France. He was a painter and sculptor and one of the founders of Cubism. He painted "Guernica" and "Les Demoiselles d'Avignon". He died in 1973.
bio|10-25|1984|Κέιτι Πέρι|Katy Perry|Katy Perry is an American singer and songwriter. She became known with hits such as "I Kissed a Girl", "Firework" and "Roar".
bio|10-25|1993|Βίνσεντ Πράις|Vincent Price|Vincent Price was an American actor, known for his roles in horror films such as "House on Haunted Hill". He died in 1993.

bio|10-26|899|Αλφρέδος ο Μέγας|Alfred the Great|Alfred the Great was king of Wessex from 871 to 899. He resisted the Vikings, protected learning and strengthened the Anglo-Saxon kingdom. He died in 899.

bio|10-26|1759|Ζωρζ Ζακ Νταντόν|Georges Danton|Georges Danton was a French politician and a leader of the French Revolution. He took part in the Committee of Public Safety. He was executed by guillotine in 1794.
bio|10-26|1890|Κάρλο Κολόντι|Carlo Collodi|Carlo Collodi was an Italian writer. He wrote the children's book "The Adventures of Pinocchio". He died in 1890.

bio|10-26|1916|Φρανσουά Μιτεράν|François Mitterrand|François Mitterrand was a French Socialist politician. He was president of France from 1981 to 1995, the longest-serving holder of the office. He died in 1996.
bio|10-26|1919|Μοχάμεντ Ρεζά Παχλαβί|Mohammad Reza Pahlavi|Mohammad Reza Pahlavi was the last shah of Iran, from 1941 to 1979. He was overthrown by the Islamic Revolution and died in 1980 in Cairo.

bio|10-26|1947|Χίλαρι Κλίντον|Hillary Clinton|Hillary Clinton is an American Democratic politician. She was First Lady, a senator for New York and Secretary of State from 2009 to 2013. She was a candidate for the presidency in 2016.
bio|10-26|1959|Έβο Μοράλες|Evo Morales|Evo Morales is a Bolivian politician. He was president of Bolivia from 2006 to 2019, the country's first indigenous president.

bio|10-26|1979|Παρκ Τζονγκ-χούι|Park Chung-hee|Park Chung-hee was a general and president of South Korea from 1961 to 1979. He was responsible for rapid economic development but also for authoritarian rule. He was assassinated in 1979.
bio|10-27|1449|Ουλούγκ Μπεγκ|Ulugh Beg|Ulugh Beg was a Timurid ruler and astronomer. He built the Samarkand Observatory and compiled an accurate catalogue of stars. He was assassinated in 1449.

bio|10-27|1782|Νικολό Παγκανίνι|Niccolò Paganini|Niccolò Paganini was an Italian violinist and composer. He is regarded as the greatest violin virtuoso of his time, known for the "24 Caprices". He died in 1840.

bio|10-27|1858|Θεόδωρος Ρούζβελτ|Theodore Roosevelt|Theodore Roosevelt was the 26th president of the United States, from 1901 to 1909. He supported the conservation of nature and in 1906 he was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize. He died in 1919.
bio|10-27|1932|Σύλβια Πλαθ|Sylvia Plath|Sylvia Plath was an American poet and writer. She wrote the novel "The Bell Jar" and the collection "Ariel". She took her own life in 1963, at the age of 30.

bio|10-27|1945|Λουίς Ινάσιο Λούλα ντα Σίλβα|Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva|Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva is a Brazilian politician and former trade unionist. He was president of Brazil from 2003 to 2010 and again from 2023.

bio|10-27|1968|Λίζε Μάιτνερ|Lise Meitner|Lise Meitner was an Austrian physicist. She contributed to the discovery of nuclear fission, but the Nobel Prize was received only by her colleague Otto Hahn. The element meitnerium bears her name. She died in 1968.

bio|10-27|2010|Νέστορ Κίρχνερ|Néstor Kirchner|Néstor Kirchner was an Argentine politician. He was president of Argentina from 2003 to 2007 and was married to Cristina Fernández de Kirchner. He died in 2010.
bio|10-27|2013|Λου Ριντ|Lou Reed|Lou Reed was an American singer-songwriter and a founding member of the Velvet Underground. He wrote hits such as "Walk on the Wild Side". He died in 2013.
bio|10-28|312|Μαξέντιος|Maxentius|Maxentius was a Roman emperor from 306 to 312. He was defeated by Constantine at the Battle of the Milvian Bridge on 28 October 312 and drowned in the Tiber.

bio|10-28|1466|Έρασμος|Erasmus|Erasmus of Rotterdam was a Dutch humanist and theologian. He wrote "In Praise of Folly" and published the first printed edition of the New Testament in Greek. The exact year of his birth is not certain. He died in 1536.

bio|10-28|1704|Τζων Λοκ|John Locke|John Locke died in 1704. He was an English philosopher and a father of liberalism, and he wrote "An Essay Concerning Human Understanding" and "Two Treatises of Government".
bio|10-28|1740|Άννα Ιβάνοβνα|Anna Ioannovna|Anna Ioannovna was empress of Russia from 1730 to 1740. Her reign was marked by the influence of German courtiers. She died in 1740.

bio|10-28|1818|Άμπιγκεϊλ Άνταμς|Abigail Adams|Abigail Adams was the wife of President John Adams and the mother of President John Quincy Adams. She is known for her letters, in which she asked that they remember "the ladies". She died in 1818.

bio|10-28|1955|Μπιλ Γκέιτς|Bill Gates|Bill Gates is an American businessman. He founded Microsoft with Paul Allen in 1975 and later founded the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, which works in health and education.

bio|10-28|1956|Μαχμούτ Αχμεντινετζάντ|Mahmoud Ahmadinejad|Mahmoud Ahmadinejad is an Iranian politician. He was president of Iran from 2005 to 2013 and was highly controversial because of the nuclear programme and his statements.
bio|10-28|1967|Τζούλια Ρόμπερτς|Julia Roberts|Julia Roberts is an American actress. She became known with the film "Pretty Woman" and won an Oscar for "Erin Brockovich".
bio|10-28|1974|Χοακίν Φίνιξ|Joaquin Phoenix|Joaquin Phoenix is an American actor. He appeared in the films "Gladiator" and "Walk the Line", and won an Oscar for his performance in "Joker".

bio|10-29|1618|Ουόλτερ Ράλεϊ|Walter Raleigh|Walter Raleigh was an English explorer, soldier and poet. He explored South America and founded a colony in Virginia. He was beheaded in 1618 on a charge of treason.

bio|10-29|1740|Τζέιμς Μπόσγουελ|James Boswell|James Boswell was a Scottish lawyer and biographer. He wrote "The Life of Samuel Johnson", which is regarded as one of the greatest biographies. He died in 1795.

bio|10-29|1783|Ζαν λε Ροντ ντ' Αλαμπέρ|Jean le Rond d'Alembert|Jean le Rond d'Alembert was a French mathematician and philosopher. He co-edited the "Encyclopédie" with Diderot and formulated d'Alembert's principle in mechanics. He died in 1783.

bio|10-29|1897|Γιόζεφ Γκαίμπελς|Joseph Goebbels|Joseph Goebbels was a German Nazi official. As Hitler's Minister of Propaganda he controlled the press and the cinema. He took his own life in 1945 in Berlin.

bio|10-29|1911|Τζόζεφ Πούλιτζερ|Joseph Pulitzer|Joseph Pulitzer was a Hungarian-American publisher and politician. He became rich through his newspapers and in his will he founded the Pulitzer Prizes. He died in 1911.

bio|10-29|1938|Έλεν Τζόνσον-Σίρλιφ|Ellen Johnson Sirleaf|Ellen Johnson Sirleaf is a Liberian politician. She was president of Liberia from 2006 to 2018, the first woman to be elected president of an African country. In 2011 she was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize.
bio|10-29|1950|Αμπντουλάχ Γκιούλ|Abdullah Gül|Abdullah Gül is a Turkish politician. He was prime minister and the 11th president of Turkey, from 2007 to 2014.
bio|10-29|1950|Γουσταύος Ε΄|Gustaf V|Gustaf V was king of Sweden from 1907 to 1950. Sweden remained neutral in both World Wars. He died in 1950.
bio|10-29|1971|Γουινόνα Ράιντερ|Winona Ryder|Winona Ryder is an American actress. She became known for the films "Edward Scissorhands" and "Little Women" and for the series "Stranger Things".

bio|10-30|1632|Κρίστοφερ Ρεν|Christopher Wren|Christopher Wren was an English architect and astronomer. He rebuilt many churches of London after the Great Fire of 1666, his greatest work being St Paul's Cathedral. He died in 1723.
bio|10-30|1735|Τζον Άνταμς|John Adams|John Adams was the 2nd president of the United States, from 1797 to 1801, and a leading figure of the American Revolution. He died on 4 July 1826.
bio|10-30|1871|Πωλ Βαλερύ|Paul Valéry|Paul Valéry was a French poet, philosopher and essayist. He wrote the poem "The Graveyard by the Sea". He died in 1945.

bio|10-30|1885|Έζρα Πάουντ|Ezra Pound|Ezra Pound was an American poet and critic. He was a pioneer of modernism and wrote the "Cantos". During the war he supported the fascist regime of Italy. He died in 1972.

bio|10-30|1910|Ερρίκος Ντυνάν|Henri Dunant|Henri Dunant was a Swiss businessman and the founder of the Red Cross. He conceived the idea when he saw the wounded at the Battle of Solferino in 1859. In 1901 he became the first to be awarded the Nobel Peace Prize. He died in 1910.

bio|10-30|1960|Ντιέγκο Μαραντόνα|Diego Maradona|Diego Maradona was an Argentine footballer and one of the greatest in history. He played for Napoli and Barcelona and led Argentina to victory in the 1986 World Cup. He died in 2020.
bio|10-30|1975|Γκούσταβ Χερτς|Gustav Hertz|Gustav Hertz died in 1975. He was a German physicist and in 1925 he shared the Nobel Prize in Physics with James Franck.

bio|10-30|2009|Κλοντ Λεβί-Στρος|Claude Lévi-Strauss|Claude Lévi-Strauss was a French anthropologist. He was the founder of structural anthropology and wrote "Tristes Tropiques". He died in 2009, at the age of 100.
bio|10-30|2010|Χάρι Μούλις|Harry Mulisch|Harry Mulisch was a Dutch writer. He wrote the novel "The Discovery of Heaven". He died in 2010.

bio|10-31|1632|Γιοχάνες Βερμέερ|Johannes Vermeer|Johannes Vermeer was a Dutch painter of the Golden Age, from Delft. He painted "Girl with a Pearl Earring", paying particular attention to light. He died in 1675.

bio|10-31|1760|Κατσουσίκα Χοκουσάι|Katsushika Hokusai|Katsushika Hokusai was a Japanese artist. He created the woodblock print "The Great Wave off Kanagawa", part of a series of views of Mount Fuji. He died in 1849.
bio|10-31|1795|Τζον Κιτς|John Keats|John Keats was an English Romantic poet. He wrote odes such as "Ode on a Grecian Urn" and "Ode to a Nightingale". He died young, in 1821, at the age of 25.

bio|10-31|1887|Τσιανγκ Κάι Σεκ|Chiang Kai-shek|Chiang Kai-shek was a Chinese military leader and politician. He led the Nationalist Party and after its defeat in the civil war in 1949 he governed Taiwan. He died in 1975.
bio|10-31|1926|Χάρρυ Χουντίνι|Harry Houdini|Harry Houdini was born in Budapest and was an American magician and escape artist. He became known for his dangerous acts. He died in 1926.
bio|10-31|1961|Πίτερ Τζάκσον|Peter Jackson|Peter Jackson is a New Zealand director. He directed the trilogy "The Lord of the Rings", which won 11 Oscars, and "The Hobbit".

bio|10-31|1984|Ίντιρα Γκάντι|Indira Gandhi|Indira Gandhi was an Indian politician. She was prime minister of India from 1966 to 1977 and again from 1980. She was assassinated in 1984 by her own bodyguards.
bio|10-31|1993|Φεντερίκο Φελίνι|Federico Fellini|Federico Fellini was an Italian director. He directed the films "La Dolce Vita", "8½" and "Amarcord", and won five Oscars. He died in 1993.

bio|10-31|2020|Σον Κόνερι|Sean Connery|Sean Connery died in 2020 in the Bahamas, at the age of 90. He was a Scottish actor and the first James Bond of the cinema. He won an Oscar for the film "The Untouchables".
bio|11-01|1636|Νικολά Μπουαλώ|Nicolas Boileau|Nicolas Boileau was a French poet and critic. In his work "The Art of Poetry" he set out the rules of French classicism. He died in 1711.
bio|11-01|1757|Αντόνιο Κανόβα|Antonio Canova|Antonio Canova was an Italian sculptor of Neoclassicism. He created "Cupid and Psyche" and the monument to Pauline Bonaparte. He died in 1822.
bio|11-01|1880|Άλφρεντ Βέγκενερ|Alfred Wegener|Alfred Wegener was a German geophysicist and meteorologist. He formulated the theory of continental drift. He died in 1930 in Greenland.

bio|11-01|1894|Αλέξανδρος Γ΄|Alexander III|Alexander III was tsar of Russia from 1881 to 1894. He was conservative and strengthened imperial power. He died in 1894 and was succeeded by his son Nicholas II.

bio|11-01|1903|Τέοντορ Μόμσεν|Theodor Mommsen|Theodor Mommsen was a German historian and jurist. He wrote "The History of Rome" and in 1902 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. He died in 1903.

bio|11-01|1924|Σουλεϊμάν Ντεμιρέλ|Süleyman Demirel|Süleyman Demirel was a Turkish politician. He was prime minister of Turkey several times and was the 9th president of the country, from 1993 to 2000. He died in 2015.
bio|11-01|1930|Άλφρεντ Βέγκενερ|Alfred Wegener|Alfred Wegener died in 1930 in Greenland, during an expedition. He was a German geophysicist who proposed the theory of continental drift.
bio|11-01|1960|Τιμ Κουκ|Tim Cook|Tim Cook is an American businessman. He has been head of Apple since 2011, when he succeeded Steve Jobs.
bio|11-01|1972|Έζρα Πάουντ|Ezra Pound|Ezra Pound died in 1972 in Venice. He was an American poet and one of the pioneers of modernism, and he wrote the "Cantos".

bio|11-02|1083|Ματθίλδη της Φλάνδρας|Matilda of Flanders|Matilda of Flanders was queen of England and the wife of William the Conqueror. She died in 1083 and was among the first people associated with the Bayeux Tapestry.
bio|11-02|1327|Ιάκωβος Β΄|James II of Aragon|James II was king of Aragon from 1291 to 1327. He conquered Sardinia and strengthened the position of Aragon in the Mediterranean. He died in 1327.
bio|11-02|1755|Μαρία Αντουανέτα|Marie Antoinette|Marie Antoinette was born in 1755 in Vienna. She was queen of France as the wife of Louis XVI and was executed in 1793.

bio|11-02|1795|Τζέιμς Νοξ Πολκ|James K. Polk|James Polk was the 11th president of the United States, from 1845 to 1849. During his term the Mexican-American War took place and the United States acquired California. He died in 1849.
bio|11-02|1815|Τζορτζ Μπουλ|George Boole|George Boole was an English mathematician and logician. He developed Boolean algebra, which is the basis of digital computers. He died in 1864.
bio|11-02|1865|Ουόρεν Χάρντινγκ|Warren Harding|Warren Harding was the 29th president of the United States, from 1921 to 1923. His administration was marked by scandals, and he died in 1923.
bio|11-02|1950|Τζορτζ Μπέρναρντ Σω|George Bernard Shaw|George Bernard Shaw died in 1950. He was an Irish playwright who wrote "Pygmalion". In 1925 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|11-02|1975|Πιερ Πάολο Παζολίνι|Pier Paolo Pasolini|Pier Paolo Pasolini was an Italian director, poet and writer. He directed the films "The Gospel According to St Matthew" and "Medea". He was murdered in Rome in 1975.
bio|11-03|361|Κωνστάντιος Β´|Constantius II|Constantius II was a Roman emperor from 337 to 361, the son of Constantine the Great. He died in 361 on his way to confront his cousin Julian.
bio|11-03|1852|Μέιτζι|Meiji|Meiji was emperor of Japan from 1867 to 1912. During his reign the country was modernised, in the "Meiji Restoration". He died in 1912.
bio|11-03|1901|Αντρέ Μαλρώ|André Malraux|André Malraux was a French writer and politician. He wrote "Man's Fate" and was Minister of Culture under de Gaulle. He died in 1976.

bio|11-03|1921|Τσαρλς Μπρονσον|Charles Bronson|Charles Bronson was an American actor. He became known for the films "The Magnificent Seven" and "The Great Escape" and for the series "Death Wish". He died in 2003.
bio|11-03|1933|Αμάρτυα Σεν|Amartya Sen|Amartya Sen is an Indian economist and philosopher. He studied poverty and development and in 1998 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Economics.

bio|11-03|1945|Γκερντ Μύλερ|Gerd Müller|Gerd Müller was a German footballer and striker. He played for Bayern Munich and won the World Cup in 1974. He was the top scorer at the 1970 World Cup. He died in 2021.

bio|11-03|1954|Ανρί Ματίς|Henri Matisse|Henri Matisse was a French painter and sculptor, the leading figure of Fauvism. He became known for his use of intense colours and simple shapes. He died in 1954.
bio|11-03|1957|Λάικα|Laika|Laika was a dog, the first animal to be placed in orbit around the Earth, on 3 November 1957, aboard the Soviet spacecraft Sputnik 2. She did not survive the mission.
bio|11-03|2024|Κουίνσι Τζόουνς|Quincy Jones|Quincy Jones was an American composer and producer. He worked with Frank Sinatra and produced Michael Jackson's "Thriller". He died in 2024.

bio|11-04|1847|Φέλιξ Μέντελσον|Felix Mendelssohn|Felix Mendelssohn was a German composer of Romanticism. He wrote "A Midsummer Night's Dream" and the "Violin Concerto", and he revived the work of Bach from oblivion. He died in 1847, at the age of 38.

bio|11-04|1916|Γουόλτερ Κρονκάιτ|Walter Cronkite|Walter Cronkite was an American television journalist. For decades he presented the CBS evening news and was regarded as "the most trusted man in America". He died in 2009.
bio|11-04|1924|Γκαμπριέλ Φωρέ|Gabriel Fauré|Gabriel Fauré was a French composer. He wrote the "Requiem" as well as many songs and chamber music. He died in 1924.
bio|11-04|1951|Τραϊάν Μπασέσκου|Traian Băsescu|Traian Băsescu is a Romanian politician. He was president of Romania from 2004 to 2014.
